cards.rule: "No" when nothing found in his record points toward ICE; "Mostly no" when at least three times as many items point the other way. Toward enforcement: 1 vote and 0 statements or actions. Against: 9 votes and 0 statements or actions.

items.t: Voted Yea on S. 2, Gallego Amdt. No. 5813: To make funds available for the timely adjudication of DACA renewal applications.. It failed 47–52; Democrats 44–0.

Voted Yea on S. 2, Motion to Waive All Applicable Budgetary Discipline Re: Baldwin Amdt. No. 5485: To redirect funding for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to the Child Care and Development Block Grant program.. It failed 46–53; Democrats 44–0.

Voted Yea on S.J.Res. 99, Motion to Proceed to S.J.Res. 99: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services relating to "Removal of the Automatic Extension of Employment Authorization Documents".. It failed 47–50; Democrats 44–0.

Voted Yea on S.Con.Res. 33, Graham Amdt. No. 5281: To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to the apprehension and deportation of adult illegal aliens convicted of rape, murder, or sexual abuse of a minor after illegally entering the United States.. It failed 98–0; Democrats 44–0.
Voted Nay on PN858, Confirmation: Markwayne Mullin, of Oklahoma, to be Secretary of Homeland Security. It failed 54–45; Democrats 2–42.
Voted Yea on H.R. 7148, Sanders Amdt. No. 4290: To rescind certain amounts appropriated for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and certain changes to Medicaid.. It failed 49–51; Democrats 45–0.
Voted Nay on PN12-40, Confirmation: Rodney Scott, of Oklahoma, to be Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Department of Homeland Security. It failed 51–46; Democrats 0–44.
Voted Nay on PN11-11, Confirmation: Kristi Noem, of South Dakota, to be Secretary of Homeland Security. It failed 59–34; Democrats 7–33.

Voted Nay on S. 5, S. 5, As Amended: A bill to require the Secretary of Homeland Security to take into custody aliens who have been charged in the United States with theft, and for other purposes.. It failed 64–35; Democrats 12–33.
Voted Nay on S. 5, Cornyn Amdt. No. 14: To expand the list of criminal offenses that subject inadmissible aliens to mandatory detention.. It failed 70–25; Democrats 21–23.

cards.rule: "Mixed" when at least 3 picked votes point each way. He cast 2 on the police or tough-on-crime side and 4 against.

items.t: Voted Yea on S. 2, Cortez Masto Amdt. No. 5463: To appropriate amounts for local law enforcement hiring programs.. It failed 45–53; Democrats 43–0.

Voted Yea on S. 2296, Van Hollen Amdt. No. 3872: To amend title 32, United States Code, to clarify certain limitations on full-time National Guard duty performed in a State, Territory, or the District of Columbia.. It failed 47–50; Democrats 44–0.
Voted Yea on S. 2296, Duckworth Amdt. No. 3210: To limit the provision of support by the Armed Forces to civilian law enforcement activities.. It failed 46–52; Democrats 44–0.
Voted Yea on S. 2296, Merkley Amdt. No. 3927: To limit the use of Federal law enforcement officers for crowd control, and for other purposes.. It failed 47–50; Democrats 44–0.

Voted Nay on S. 331, S. 331, as amended: A bill to amend the Controlled Substances Act with respect to the scheduling of fentanyl-related substances, and for other purposes.. It failed 84–16; Democrats 30–15.

Voted Yea on S.Con.Res. 7, Lujan Amdt. No. 699: To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to supporting police, which may include initiatives that provide funding directly to law enforcement agencies to hire or rehire additional career law enforcement officers in an effort to increase their community policing capacity and crime prevention efforts.. It failed 48–52; Democrats 45–0.

cards.rule: His votes decide the headline: 0 of the 7 business, finance and labor votes picked went the business way (a third or fewer is "Mostly no", two thirds or more "Mostly yes"). With none, it is "Mostly no" rather than "No" because other items, such as corporate PAC money, point the business way.

items.t: Voted Nay on taking up the CLARITY Act, the crypto industry's market-structure bill (H.R. 3633). It failed 49–50; Democrats 0–44.
Took $50,000 from 22 corporate PACs in 2025–26, compared with $25,500 in 2023–24.
Took $12,000 from trade associations and cooperatives in 2025–26.
Labor PACs gave $12,500 in 2025–26, compared with $50,000 from corporate PACs.
Voted Nay on the GENIUS Act regulating payment stablecoins (S. 1582). It failed 68–30; Democrats 18–26.
Voted Nay on repealing the Comptroller of the Currency's bank-merger review rule (S.J.Res. 13). It failed 52–47; Democrats 0–45.
Voted Nay on repealing the IRS rule requiring crypto brokers to report users' sales (H.J.Res. 25). It failed 70–28; Democrats 17–26.
Voted Nay on repealing the consumer bureau's rule on big-tech payment apps (S.J.Res. 28). It failed 51–47; Democrats 0–44.
Voted Nay on repealing the consumer bureau's overdraft-fee rule (S.J.Res. 18). It failed 52–48; Democrats 0–45.
Voted Nay on repealing the EPA's methane fee on oil and gas producers (H.J.Res. 35). It failed 52–47; Democrats 0–45.
